name: single_review
description: Declared-requirement document-evidence triage with exact citations and an optional injected validation reviewer.

input_contract.root: Object with requirements and documents lists; optional nonblank label.
input_contract.requirement: Unique nonblank id, description, integer priority 1..5 (1 highest), evidence_rules.
input_contract.document: Unique nonblank id, string text, optional nonblank title. Empty text is allowed.
input_contract.evidence_rules: all_of, any_of, contradicts are optional lists of nonblank case-sensitive literal strings. At least one positive term is required. Duplicate terms across or within positive groups, and identical positive/contradictory terms, are rejected.

status_rules.supported: All all_of terms and at least one any_of term (if supplied) occur anywhere across supplied documents, with no contradictory term.
status_rules.partial: Some positive terms occur but the complete positive rule is not met, with no contradictory term.
status_rules.missing: No positive or contradictory term occurs. Absence is not proof of failure.
status_rules.conflicting: At least one declared contradicts term occurs, even if positive evidence is absent. Requires human resolution, not a failure verdict.

citations: All literal occurrences, including overlaps, with document_id, exact quote, rule, term, zero-based Unicode character start and exclusive end.
gap_order: Declared priority ascending, then conflicting/missing/partial, then requirement ID. Each gap links to a requirement ID, finding status, and exact citations.
reviewer: Python API analyze(data, reviewer=None). Callback receives a deep-copied bundle with requirements, documents, findings; returns all findings. IDs, statuses, exact spans, rules, and evidence completeness are checked. Reordering permitted; changing deterministic evidence outcomes rejected. Callback exceptions reject the report.
fictional_notice: All examples and test fixtures are fictional; they do not encode legal standards.
limitations: Literal matching only; cannot understand paraphrase, negation, applicability, chronology, or document authenticity.
Terms can match substrings; authors must select sufficiently specific literals and explicit contradiction rules.
Evidence may be combined across documents; no same-document co-occurrence requirement is inferred.
Conflicts are surfaced, not automatically resolved; no document is assumed more authoritative or current.
Supplied input is local JSON only; no extraction, network, paid providers, or persistence service.
No legal or compliance certification, and no conclusion that missing evidence proves failure.
Injected callbacks are trusted local Python code, not sandboxed; validation constrains returned findings, not callback side effects.
No resource limits for very large documents or highly repetitive terms.
measurement: Token usage is measured externally by the parent; no usage, cost, finance, or rating estimates are asserted.
